headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Energy Users
short_summary: This bill requires large energy users, such as data centers, to pay for their increased grid capacity costs, aiming to reduce residential utility bills.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocates, environmental groups.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial users.
news_headline: Governor amends bills that shift costs onto data centers. Critics say her tweaks weaken them.
news_summary: Governor Spanberger suggested amendments to HB 1393 and SB 253, which aim to shift grid costs to high-load users like data centers to save residential customers money and expand a power line burial program. Critics argue the governor's tweaks weaken the original intent of the bills, which were designed to make data centers shoulder more energy costs.

headline: Mandate Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water suppliers to report the total volume of water provided to data centers, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board for better resource planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservationists, local governments, policymakers.
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Approve Legislation to Track Water Use by Data Centers Across Virginia
news_summary: Virginia lawmakers passed SB 553 to strengthen water-use reporting requirements for data centers, ensuring better data on water consumption as the industry expands. This legislation addresses concerns about the lack of centralized tracking of data center water use, which can involve millions of gallons daily for cooling servers.

headline: Regulate Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for new high energy use facilities, including noise profiles and potential impacts on local resources, before local approval.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, environmental groups, historic preservation advocates, local governments.
news_headline: A Roanoke Delegate Helped Write Virginia's New Data Center Law. Here's What It Does, and What It Doesn't
news_summary: Virginia's new law, HB 153, requires developers of large data centers to conduct site assessments for noise and utilities to disclose substation needs before local approval. However, the law mandates studies but does not set specific limits on noise, water usage, or setbacks.
